children.text: Water and Objects

Study water surface tension \(\gamma\), water density \(\rho\), and gravity \(g\). Atmospheric pressure \(P_0\) is uniform. For the board and rods, the undisturbed far surface is \(z=0\). Configurations are invariant along y. Surface slope angle \(\theta(x)\) is measured counterclockwise from positive x. Except where specified, no small-slope approximation is assumed.
A.1. Coalescing drop jump

Two spherical drops of radius \(a=100\,\mathrm{\mu m}\) merge on a superhydrophobic surface. The merged drop is spherical and volume is conserved. Fraction \(k=0.06\) of released surface energy becomes jump kinetic energy. Use \(\rho=1.00\times10^3\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}\), \(\gamma=7.27\times10^{-2}\,\mathrm{J/m^2}\). Find initial jump speed to two significant figures.

The surface obeys \(\tfrac12(z/\ell)^a+\cos\theta=\mathrm{constant}\). Find \(a\) and \(\ell\), for either hydrophilic or hydrophobic boards.

statement.text:
Water and Objects
Study water surface tension \(\gamma\), water density \(\rho\), and gravity \(g\). Atmospheric pressure \(P_0\) is uniform. For the board and rods, the undisturbed far surface is \(z=0\). Configurations are invariant along y. Surface slope angle \(\theta(x)\) is measured counterclockwise from positive x. Except where specified, no small-slope approximation is assumed.
A.1. Coalescing drop jump
Two spherical drops of radius \(a=100\,\mathrm{\mu m}\) merge on a superhydrophobic surface. The merged drop is spherical and volume is conserved. Fraction \(k=0.06\) of released surface energy becomes jump kinetic energy. Use \(\rho=1.00\times10^3\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}\), \(\gamma=7.27\times10^{-2}\,\mathrm{J/m^2}\). Find initial jump speed to two significant figures.
B.1. Hydrostatic pressure

A thin vertical board lies in the yz-plane. In the hydrophilic case the water surface rises at the board. Find water pressure at height \(z\).
B.2. Pressure force on a surface block

A cutout water block has water-surface edge heights \(z_1\) on the left and \(z_2\) on the right. Find the net horizontal pressure force per unit y-length. Uniform atmospheric pressure contributes no net force.
B.3. Surface tension balance
The surface angles at these edges are \(\theta_1,\theta_2\). Express the same pressure force using surface tension.
B.4. Capillary first integral
The surface obeys \(\tfrac12(z/\ell)^a+\cos\theta=\mathrm{constant}\). Find \(a\) and \(\ell\), for either hydrophilic or hydrophobic boards.
B.5. Small-slope meniscus
Assume \(|z^{\prime}(x)|\ll1\). Expand the cosine to second order, derive the differential equation and solve for \(x\ge0\), given \(z^{\prime}(0)=\tan\theta_0\) and \(z(\infty)=0\).
C.1. Force on the right rod

Two identical parallel rods float symmetrically about the y-axis. For right rod B, let the inner and outer contacts have heights \(z_a,z_b\), and tangent-angle magnitudes \(\theta_a,\theta_b\), as shown. Find the horizontal force per unit y-length.
C.2. Force from midpoint height
The surface at the midpoint between rods has height \(z_0\). Express \(F_x\) without using either contact height or angle.
C.3. Midpoint level
Let the inner contact of right rod B be \((x_a,z_a)\). Use the small-slope equation to find \(z_0\).

children.text: Water and Objects
A.1. Coalescing drop jump
The new radius is \(2^{1/3}a\), mass \(8\pi\rho a^3/3\), and released surface energy \(4\pi\gamma a^2(2-2^{2/3})\). Hence \[v=\sqrt{\frac{3k\gamma(2-2^{2/3})}{\rho a}}=0.23\,\mathrm{m/s}.\]
B.1. Hydrostatic pressure
Hydrostatic equilibrium gives \(P=P_0-\rho gz\), including negative gauge pressure above the far surface.
B.2. Pressure force on a surface block
Integrate the gauge pressure on the two faces: \[f_x=\frac12\rho g(z_2^2-z_1^2).\] In the illustrated hydrophilic case this is negative, towards the board.
B.3. Surface tension balance
Surface tension on the block has component \(\gamma(\cos\theta_2-\cos\theta_1)\). Force balance gives \[f_x=\gamma(\cos\theta_1-\cos\theta_2).\]
B.4. Capillary first integral

Combine B2 and B3: \(\rho gz^2/2+\gamma\cos\theta\) is constant, equal to \(\gamma\) far away. Therefore \(a=2\) and \(\ell=\sqrt{\gamma/(\rho g)}\). Gravity is required in \(\ell\), although it is omitted from one parameter list in the source.
B.5. Small-slope meniscus

Use \(\cos\theta\simeq1-(z^{\prime})^2/2\) to get \(z^2/\ell^2-(z^{\prime})^2=0\). Differentiate to obtain \(z^{\prime\prime}=z/\ell^2\). The decaying solution is \[z(x)=-\ell\tan\theta_0e^{-x/\ell}.\]
C.1. Force on the right rod

Pressure integration gives \(\rho g(z_b^2-z_a^2)/2\), and surface tension gives \(\gamma(\cos\theta_b-\cos\theta_a)\). Therefore \[F_x=\frac{\rho g}{2}(z_b^2-z_a^2)+\gamma(\cos\theta_b-\cos\theta_a).\]
C.2. Force from midpoint height

At the midpoint, symmetry gives \(\theta=0\). The outer surface tends to \(z=0,\theta=0\). Apply the first integral separately inside and outside to C1: \[F_x=-\frac12\rho gz_0^2.\] The force is attractive.
C.3. Midpoint level
Symmetry sets the two exponential coefficients equal, so \(z(x)=z_0\cosh(x/\ell)\). Thus \[z_0=\frac{z_a}{\cosh(x_a/\ell)}=\frac{2z_a}{e^{x_a/\ell}+e^{-x_a/\ell}}.\]

Water and Objects
A.1. Coalescing drop jump
The new radius is \(2^{1/3}a\), mass \(8\pi\rho a^3/3\), and released surface energy \(4\pi\gamma a^2(2-2^{2/3})\). Hence \[v=\sqrt{\frac{3k\gamma(2-2^{2/3})}{\rho a}}=0.23\,\mathrm{m/s}.\]
B.1. Hydrostatic pressure
Hydrostatic equilibrium gives \(P=P_0-\rho gz\), including negative gauge pressure above the far surface.
B.2. Pressure force on a surface block
Integrate the gauge pressure on the two faces: \[f_x=\frac12\rho g(z_2^2-z_1^2).\] In the illustrated hydrophilic case this is negative, towards the board.
B.3. Surface tension balance
Surface tension on the block has component \(\gamma(\cos\theta_2-\cos\theta_1)\). Force balance gives \[f_x=\gamma(\cos\theta_1-\cos\theta_2).\]
B.4. Capillary first integral
Combine B2 and B3: \(\rho gz^2/2+\gamma\cos\theta\) is constant, equal to \(\gamma\) far away. Therefore \(a=2\) and \(\ell=\sqrt{\gamma/(\rho g)}\). Gravity is required in \(\ell\), although it is omitted from one parameter list in the source.
B.5. Small-slope meniscus

C.1. Force on the right rod

C.2. Force from midpoint height
At the midpoint, symmetry gives \(\theta=0\). The outer surface tends to \(z=0,\theta=0\). Apply the first integral separately inside and outside to C1: \[F_x=-\frac12\rho gz_0^2.\] The force is attractive.
C.3. Midpoint level
Symmetry sets the two exponential coefficients equal, so \(z(x)=z_0\cosh(x/\ell)\). Thus \[z_0=\frac{z_a}{\cosh(x_a/\ell)}=\frac{2z_a}{e^{x_a/\ell}+e^{-x_a/\ell}}.\]
